page.layout: One printed page of running text, one column. Running head and page number at the top. Canon references (23.q.4., 28.q.1., 30.q.5.) open paragraphs in the text column. Two italic argument titles stand centred between paragraphs. A single gathering mark at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Et mox. Deus masculum & foeminam pro-pagandi generis causa nuptiali castitate coniun-xit, & secundas nuptias, quae in utroque Testa-mento permittuntur, licitas esse monstravit.

Item idem. Quod si dormierit vir eius, non dicit primus, vel secundus, vel quartus, nec no-bis diffiniendū est, quod non diffiniuit Apofto-lus. Vnde nec villas debeo damnare nuptias, nec eis verecundiam inferre numerositatis. Domi-nus autem septemuirarii[?] non damnauit.

23.q.4. Quod autem.) Post mortem Sarae Abraham Cethuram duxit uxorem, ne secundum Augusti. Christiani putarent esse peccatum post mortem uxoris aliam ducere. Et mox idem ex Augusti. lib.2. contra aduersarium Legis & Pro-phetarum.
28.q.1. Caue. (Caue Christiane gentili aut Iudaeo filiam tuam tradere. Caue inquit gentilem vel Iudaeam atq; alienigenam, hoc est, omnem haereticam & alienam à fide tua accipere tibi uxorem, &c.
30[?].q.5. Aliter.) Aliter legitimum non sit con[?]

page.notes: Printed text ends with "con" at the line end and a single mark "I" centred below it; read as a gathering signature. The canon number "30.q.5." is uncertain (the first digit could be 10 or 30). "Augusti." is read from a ligatured "ft" and may be a printing variant. "septemuirarii" is uncertain at the first syllable, marked [?]. Long s rendered as plain s throughout.
